# dsh-conv-calendar
**English** | 中文
A GitHub-style contribution calendar for DeepSeek Harness — see how many prompts you sent, how many
conversations you had, and how many tokens you burned, one square per day.
## Features
- **A sidebar entry.** *Conversation calendar* appears in the Web GUI sidebar; clicking it opens a f

ull-page calendar.
- **GitHub-style grid.** The whole current calendar year — always a full year of
squares, padded out to whole Monday-started weeks, future days included — five shades, one square pe

r local day.
- **Four metrics.** Switch between **Prompts**, **Conversations**, **Tokens** and **Out

l day.
- **Four metrics.** Switch between **Prompts**, **Conversations**, **Tokens** and **Output**:
| Metric | What one square means |

| Prompts | How many messages you sent that day |
| Conversations | How many sessions were active th

at day |
| Tokens | Total tokens spent that day (input + output + cache reads) |
| Output | Tokens t
he model produced that day |
- **Four stat cards.** This year's total (with active days), current streak (with longest), this mon
th (with last month), this year's busiest day — all of them follow the selected metric. The card fig
ures use the same year scope as the grid; only the streaks keep the full history, because a run can

cross 1 January.
- **Token breakdown.** Under *Tokens* and *Output*, hovering a square also shows th

e `input · output · cached` split; hovering a future square shows its date alone.
- **Theme-aware.**

Colors come from DSH theme variables, so light and dark mode both look native.
- **Bilingual.** Fol
lows the UI language (English / Chinese).
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** or a compatible build (it relies on the `sidebar.panellist` and `m

ain` slots, and on `ctx.sessionQuery`).
- Node **22.15+** on the Host side (the session logs are zst

d on `ctx.sessionQuery`).
- Node **22.15+** on the Host side (the session logs are zstd-compressed).
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart DeepSeek Harness**. Plugins are composed from the profile's bundle list at startup, s
o a restart is required — the entry cannot hot-load into a running Host.
After the restart:

1. A *Conversation calendar* icon appears in the sidebar;
2. Opening it shows history already filled
in, and today's square darkens as you send new messages.
To uninstall:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> If a plugin ever prevents the app from starting, remove the `"dsh-conv-calendar"` line from `dsh.p
rofile.bundles` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/package.json` instead of using the recovery dialog, wh
ich also resets unrelated settings.
## What gets counted
### Prompts
A message counts only when all three hold:

1. the session event is `user/message`;
2. `data.source.kind === 'user'` — i.e. **you** sent it. Inj
ected context (runtime context, skill catalog, time context, tool reminders …) carries its own sourc

e and is never counted;
3. it falls on a given day in the **machine's local time zone**.
### Tokens
Taken from `data.usage` on `assistant/message` events:
| Field | Meaning |

| `inputTokens` | Input tokens that missed the cache |
| `outputTokens` | Tokens the model produced

|
| `cacheReadTokens` | Input tokens served from the cache |
| `totalTokens` | Sum of the three (pro
vider-reported; summed locally when absent) |
Older log entries may omit `cacheReadTokens` (treated as `0`); replies with no `usage` at all are sk
log entries may omit `cacheReadTokens` (treated as `0`); replies with no `usage` at all are skipped.
### Cross-session de-duplication
Forking a session copies its ancestor's log. A copied prompt or reply keeps the same `message.id`, s
o hashing it lands in the same set and is counted once. That also makes re-reading a log idempotent
— re-scanning can never double count.
> **Active days can differ per metric.** A day where the model replied but you sent nothing counts u
nder *Tokens* but not under *Prompts*. That is intended.
## Where the data comes from
| Source | Used for | Notes |
| `session/event` feed | Live counting | Every new message, and every reply carrying `usage`, is rec

orded immediately — no waiting for a disk flush |
| `ctx.sessionQuery` (`listSessions` / `readSessio
n`) | Backfill | History is read through the Host's own decoder: the logs are appended frame by fram
e, so a single whole-file `zstdDecompressSync` only yields the first frame |
A finished session is read once and marked `final`; it is never re-read. A session that is still liv
e is re-read on every refresh and **merged** (union of hashes, so it is idempotent). One backfill pa
ss has an 8-second budget — leftovers resume on the next pass.
### State file
`$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-conv-calendar/state.json`, written atomically (temp file + rename):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`version` is the store layout: `1` kept a bare array of prompt hashes per day, `2` adds `replies`. A
n incompatible version is **dropped and fully re-read** — the file is only a cache, so one pass rebu
atible version is **dropped and fully re-read** — the file is only a cache, so one pass rebuilds it.
Deleting the file clears the statistics; they are rebuilt from the session logs on the next start.

The panel reads one read-only endpoint from the same Host process:

The response is JSON:

## Limitations
- **Backfill needs `sessionQuery`.** In a composition without it, only the current run is counted an

d the footer says so.
- **Finished sessions are never re-read.** That is safe because a finished log

cannot change; if you rewrite history by hand, delete `state.json`.
- **Only human messages count.*

* Injected context never does — that is the point.
- **The time zone is the machine's, read at start
up.** After travelling, old dates stay filed under the local date they happened on.
